articles.title: Childhood trauma is linked to suicidal thoughts and attempts in adults with depression and anxiety
articles.summary: Among Dutch adults with depression or anxiety, those who experienced more childhood trauma were more likely to report recent suicidal thoughts and past suicide attempts. Aggression, insomnia, and low social support partly accounted for this link.

articles.title: Americans’ support for political violence fell in 2026, but MAGA supporters remain the most likely to justify it
articles.summary: A new survey finds that American support for political violence decreased heading into the 2026 midterms. While MAGA supporters remain the most likely to justify violence, overall willingness to commit physical harm dropped across the ideological spectrum.

articles.title: New study identifies four unique migraine phenotypes using artificial intelligence
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence can accurately identify migraine sufferers by analyzing general health data like sleep and neck pain, completely ignoring headache symptoms. The findings suggest migraines consist of several distinct biological subtypes that could require different medical treatments.

articles.title: Travel Time Prediction in Supply Chain Management Using Machine Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.38190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of this research is to find data and methods using machine learning and deep learning to correctly predict the estimated travel time for transportation and logistics in a supply chain system. The supply chain ecosystem is very complex and heavily relies on the transportation and logistics of raw materials and finished goods. Accurate travel time estimation is critical because it helps supply chain members to improve logistics consistency and performance. articles.title: EHR2Trace: Auditable EHR Data Infrastructure for Patient World Models and Clinical Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.38193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Patient world models and clinical agents aim to predict changes in patients' health and support clinical work. Developing these systems requires reliable histories of patient conditions, treatments, and the information available at each decision. Electronic health records (EHRs) contain these histories, but differences in how events are recorded make them difficult to use consistently. We present EHR2Trace, a system that converts EHRs from different sources into traceable patient events for model training and evaluation. It links events to source

articles.title: Early-life sugar restriction tied to better mental health in adulthood
articles.summary: A recent study using the end of post-war UK food rationing suggests that restricting sugar from conception to age two is linked to a significantly lower risk of developing anxiety and depression in adulthood.

articles.title: People found not guilty by reason of insanity show a surprisingly mixed criminal risk profile
articles.summary: Psychiatric symptoms alone do not explain why some people with mental illness enter the criminal justice system. A new study reveals that standard criminal risk factors, like antisocial attitudes and social environments, closely mirror their legal involvement.

articles.title: Excitement from a virtual reality game spills over into men’s romantic judgments, study finds
articles.summary: Can an elevated heart rate trick you into feeling attraction? New research indicates that men, but not women, tend to carry over physical excitement from a thrilling virtual reality game into their online dating decisions.

articles.title: Losing deep belly fat may slow brain aging and protect memory
articles.summary: Losing deep belly fat rather than just overall body weight is linked to slower brain aging and better memory years later. New research suggests targeting visceral fat might protect cognitive function by improving long-term blood sugar control.

articles.title: This diet may slow brain aging by 2.5 years
articles.summary: People who followed the MIND diet more closely showed slower brain shrinkage and less grey matter loss over time, with the strongest differences equivalent to about 2.5 years of delayed brain aging. Berries and poultry were linked with healthier brain changes, while sweets and fried fast foods were associated with greater tissue loss.

articles.title: Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may have a reversible weakness
articles.summary: The Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may actively damage brain blood vessels and sabotage the cellular systems that remove harmful proteins. Researchers were able to reverse some of these effects in experiments, revealing promising new targets for Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and other neurodegenerative diseases.
